title: Truncation diagnosis at 2048/3072, then a scoring-rule and token-budget change BEFORE any formal cell was generated
stage: after the 35-item (5-per-size) alpha=0 preflight was run at max_new_tokens=2048 and re-run at 3072; BEFORE any --mode formal cell (280 items, non-zero alpha) exists for either model
code_changes: zebralogic/get_answer_zebralogic.py: ALLOWED_MAX_NEW_TOKENS extended from (2048, 3072) to (1024, 2048, 3072). 4096 remains out of scope.

zebralogic/official_zebra_grid_scorer.py: UNCHANGED (see revision_r1 below -- an earlier draft of this amendment edited this file directly; it was restored to byte-identical content with commit 57ea959).

zebralogic/first_answer_scorer.py (NEW FILE): score_one_item_first (identical no-answer/cell-comparison rules to score_one_item, but extracts via commitment_metrics.find_first_answer_json -- first complete JSON carrying a non-empty dict "solution" -- instead of the official BACKWARD-scanning extract_last_complete_json).

zebralogic/commitment_metrics.py: added find_first_answer_json (see revision_r1 below); compute_commitment_metrics switched from find_first_complete_json to find_first_answer_json for the same reason score_one_item_first needed it. find_first_complete_json itself is UNCHANGED.

zebralogic/eval_zebralogic.py: score_rows() now calls score_one_item_first as MAIN (parsed/solved/correct_cells/cell_rate/no_answer) and score_one_item as a parallel sensitivity readout (*_last fields). summarize() adds puzzle_acc_last/cell_acc_last/no_answer_rate_last (overall) and no_answer_rate per size in by_size. cmd_preflight_check and cmd_formal print both the MAIN (FIRST-JSON) table and a LAST-JSON sensitivity table, plus a per-size no_answer_rate breakdown. first_final_grid_agreement / revision_wrong_to_right / revision_right_to_wrong are UNCHANGED -- they still compare FIRST vs LAST regardless of which one is MAIN, since they are revision-detection metrics, not accuracy readouts.
context: The 2048-token alpha=0 preflight (35 items, 5 per size) showed Llama-3.1-8B at 12/35 (34%) unparsed+truncated: the generation reaches max_new_tokens with no complete JSON object at all. Re-running at 3072 changed nothing (still 12/35) -- diagnose_truncation.py's per-row tails show these are answer-formation-time loops (the model repeats already-established facts in a closed cycle and never reaches the point of writing a solution key), not a token-budget shortfall. Of the 23 Llama rows that DO produce a complete JSON, all 23 complete their FIRST JSON well before 350 tokens; all 35 Qwen2.5-7B rows complete their first JSON before 400 tokens and never fail to produce one. Given this, the user made two decisions: (1) score the FIRST complete JSON as MAIN (a puzzle with no first-JSON answer is scored incorrect, with no_answer_rate reported explicitly, including per size, as its own diagnostic -- rather than silently retrying a later, possibly loop-contaminated JSON); (2) lower the token budget to 1024, since neither of the two observed failure modes (fast completion; pre-answer loop) is helped by a larger budget, and 1024 leaves ample headroom above the observed maxima while running much faster than 2048/3072.
why_first_not_last: The official scorer (score_one_item / extract_last_complete_json) grades the LAST complete JSON in the text. On a generation that loops after answering, or loops WITHOUT ever answering but happens to emit a syntactically-complete (if wrong) JSON block late in the loop, LAST-JSON scoring can credit or blame a state the model reached only through post-answer repetition, not through the reasoning process itself. Scoring FIRST matches what "the model's answer" means for a commitment-timing analysis: it is the earliest point at which the model produced a complete, gradeable answer, before any later revision. This mirrors the standing FIRST=MAIN convention already used elsewhere in this repo for exactly this reason (P4c CRUXEval-O: 'FIRST stays MAIN... a decoding artifact is a parser bug; a model failing the format is a result').
why_last_is_kept: LAST-JSON (official) scoring is retained as a parallel sensitivity readout (*_last fields, a separate printed table) to quantify first/last drift -- never as the primary claim. This lets a reader see, per alpha, whether steering changes how much the model revises its answer after first committing one, without conflating that revision behavior with the primary accuracy claim.
why_no_answer_is_reported_not_silently_f: no_answer_rate (overall and per size) is now printed explicitly wherever puzzle_acc is printed, because a no-answer item and a wrong-but-complete-JSON item are different failure modes that puzzle_acc (both count as 'not solved') cannot distinguish. This also makes it possible to observe, descriptively, whether steering changes how often the model ever completes a first JSON at all -- a question the pre-amendment scoring could not separate from puzzle accuracy.
why_1024_not_2048_or_3072: Measured at the 3072 preflight re-run (both models, n=35 each): Llama's 23 parsed rows all complete their first JSON in well under 350 tokens; its 12 unparsed rows never complete one even at 3072 (confirmed unchanged from 2048, so more tokens does not help them). Qwen's 35 rows all complete their first JSON in well under 400 tokens. 1024 is therefore not a compromise -- it exceeds every observed completion point in the diagnosed preflight batch by a wide margin, and no plausible mechanism (a pre-answer loop; a fast, well-formed answer) benefits from 2048 or 3072 over 1024. This is a SPEED gain, not a scientific tradeoff: unparsed+truncated rows are diagnosed as an answer-formation-time failure, not a budget-limited one.
why_1024_2048_3072_stay_the_allowed_set_: 1024 is ADDED, not a replacement for 2048/3072 -- ALLOWED_MAX_NEW_TOKENS keeps all three so a future re-diagnosis is not blocked from re-running the earlier budgets. 4096 remains explicitly out of scope per the original prereg S3 and is unaffected by this amendment; nothing in the truncation diagnosis argues for raising the ceiling above 3072, since the failure mode that would motivate that (a genuinely token-budget-limited answer) was not observed.

llama3_3072.note: identical unparsed count to 2048 -- confirms the 12 rows are not token-budget-limited

qwen25_3072.note: 35/35 always produce a complete first JSON

unchanged: item set, item order, sample_id assignment, EXPECTED_EASY_IDS_SHA256
PROTOCOL tag ("zebralogic-easy-v0") -- item/dose identity is untouched, only scoring rule and token budget change, hence an additive amendment rather than a new protocol tag
batch_size=8, temperature=0.0, top_p=1.0, prefill_tail_len=1, no chat template
Holm m=3 per model, McNemar/bootstrap conventions, workpoint rule (prereg section 8)

is_strict_loop, grid_is_fully_specified, first_final_grid_agreement -- unchanged. solution_first_rate/first_solution_pos/pre_solution_chars now anchor on find_first_answer_json rather than find_first_complete_json (see revision_r1); this is a bugfix to what these metrics were always meant to measure ('first answer'), not a redefinition.

existing_cell_is_valid()'s config-mismatch guard -- a 2048/3072 preflight cell is never silently rescored or overwritten as a 1024 cell; a fresh 1024 preflight/formal cell must be generated to a NEW path (mode/alpha/max_new_tokens all recorded in meta and checked)
next_step: Re-run the 35-item alpha=0 preflight at max_new_tokens=1024 for both models (fresh cell, since 1024 was not previously an allowed budget and no existing file at that budget exists) and score it with the new FIRST-JSON scoring to confirm the amended scoring/budget behave as expected before any formal 280-item, non-zero-alpha sweep is launched.

revision_r1.reviewer_note: Three corrections made before any preflight was run under this amendment -- review caught them pre-execution, not after seeing biased results.

corrections.issue: "first complete JSON" is not the same as "first answer". find_first_complete_json (used by the original score_one_item_first) returns the first SYNTACTICALLY complete top-level JSON object with no check on its contents. If a model emits some other complete JSON object before the one carrying "solution" (a partial restatement, an intermediate structure), that earlier answer-less block would be scored as the item's answer -- reading as "no answer" (or scoring an unrelated empty prediction_table) while a real answer follows later in the same text.
corrections.fix: Added commitment_metrics.find_first_answer_json: scans the same complete-JSON blocks as find_first_complete_json but skips any block lacking a non-empty dict "solution" key, returning the first block that has one. score_one_item_first now uses find_first_answer_json, not find_first_complete_json. compute_commitment_metrics (solution_first_rate, first_solution_pos, pre_solution_chars, etc.) was ALSO switched from find_first_complete_json to find_first_answer_json for the same reason -- those metrics were built to describe "first answer" behavior and had the identical bug. find_first_complete_json itself is UNCHANGED and is still used where "first complete JSON regardless of content" is genuinely the right question (zebralogic/diagnose_truncation.py's truncation diagnosis, which is unrelated to answer content).
corrections.test_added: test_find_first_answer_json (commitment_metrics-level) and an added case in test_score_one_item_first_vs_last (scorer-level): an answer-less JSON object followed by a real answer JSON must be scored as the real answer, not as no-answer. Also covers an empty-dict "solution" (vacuously present but not a real answer) being skipped the same way.

corrections.issue: official_zebra_grid_scorer.py, which docs/PREREG_ZEBRALOGIC_EASY.md section 2 describes as ported VERBATIM from WildEval/ZeroEval for auditability against its upstream source, had been directly edited to add score_prediction_table and score_one_item_first alongside the original extract_last_complete_json/score_one_item/build_solution_table.
corrections.fix: official_zebra_grid_scorer.py was restored to byte-identical content with commit 57ea959 (its state before this amendment's first draft) -- verified by diff. All first-answer scoring logic (score_one_item_first) moved to a new file, zebralogic/first_answer_scorer.py, which imports find_first_answer_json from commitment_metrics.py and reproduces score_one_item's cell-comparison rules directly (not by importing score_prediction_table from the official file, since that helper no longer exists there) rather than importing anything project-specific into the official port.
corrections.verification: diff between commit 57ea959's official_zebra_grid_scorer.py and the restored file is empty (151 lines, byte-identical).

corrections.issue: The planned 1024-token preflight re-run would write to the SAME _preflight/mdf_0 path as the existing 2048/3072 cells. existing_cell_is_valid()'s config-mismatch guard (correctly) hard-stops rather than silently regenerating over a differently-configured existing file -- so running the 1024 preflight without first moving the old directory out of the way reproduces the exact FAIL this amendment's own diagnosis process already hit once (max_new_tokens 2048 vs 3072 mismatch).
corrections.fix: The server run order (given to the user) now moves the existing _preflight directory to _preflight_3072_backup (matching the mv-before-rerun pattern already used for the 2048->3072 escalation) BEFORE launching the 1024 preflight, for both models, using each model's own OUT_ROOT (llama3: components/llama3/zebralogic_easy; qwen2.5: components/qwen2.5/zebralogic_easy, both under BASE_DIR which defaults to /data1/paveen/Dopamine/components on the server).

revision_r1.scope_correction: The 35-item (5-per-size) preflight sample establishes that max_new_tokens=1024 is adequate for THOSE 35 items only. It does NOT establish, and must not be cited as establishing, that the budget is adequate for the remaining 245 items in the 280-item formal set -- those items were never generated at any budget and their length distribution is unobserved. Formal-sweep results under the 1024 budget must be reported as "performance under a 1024-token first-answer budget", not as equivalent to a result obtained at 2048/3072 -- the two are not established to be interchangeable outside the diagnosed 35-item preflight sample.

revision_r2.reviewer_note: Two remaining small issues, found by review after revision_r1 was frozen and before any preflight was run under this amendment.

corrections.issue: revision_r1's own correction[0].fix text asserted find_first_complete_json 'is still used where first complete JSON regardless of content is genuinely the right question (zebralogic/diagnose_truncation.py's truncation diagnosis, which is unrelated to answer content)' -- but at the time that text was written, diagnose_truncation.py's field names (has_solution_json, first_solution_end_token, solution_completed_before_limit, loop_before_solution/loop_after_solution) still implied ANSWER content, while the code computing them was still find_first_complete_json-based (unfixed). The r1 text was descriptively wrong about the script's own state, not merely stale.
corrections.fix: diagnose_truncation.py now computes and reports BOTH notions as two clearly separated field sets, rather than picking one: has_first_json/first_json_end_char/first_json_end_token/trailing_tokens_after_json/json_completed_before_limit/loop_before_json/loop_after_json (GENERIC, find_first_complete_json -- any content) alongside has_answer_json/first_answer_end_char/first_answer_end_token/trailing_tokens_after_answer/answer_completed_before_limit/loop_before_answer/loop_after_answer (ANSWER, find_first_answer_json -- non-empty dict solution). The printed summary's PRIMARY bucketing (answered+truncated / unanswered+truncated / etc.) and per-row divergence count (first_json_vs_answer_json_divergent_n) are on the ANSWER fields, since 'was the puzzle answered before the limit' is the diagnostic's actual purpose; the GENERIC fields are printed alongside so a divergence is visible rather than silently absorbed.
corrections.verification: Re-ran diagnose_truncation.py against the already-collected llama3 3072-token preflight cell: 0/35 rows show first-JSON/answer-JSON divergence in that batch (the earlier single-field version happened not to have been fooled on this particular data), and the answered/unanswered counts (23/12) reproduce exactly what the pre-fix version reported for that batch -- confirming the fix changes no historical conclusion, only closes the gap for any future batch where the two notions do diverge. A synthetic fake-tokenizer test (answer-less JSON, then a real answer JSON, then a loop after the answer) confirms has_first_json/has_answer_json correctly diverge and first_json_end_char < first_answer_end_char when they do.

corrections.issue: zebralogic/run_zebralogic.sh's cmd_preflight comments still said 'the 5 fixed items' (stale: the frozen preflight sample is 35 items, 5 per size, across all 7 easy sizes -- corrected in the code itself on 2026-09-04, but the launcher's own comments were never updated) and 'max_new_tokens is still hard-enforced to {2048,3072}' (stale after this amendment added 1024). A comment this wrong about a FROZEN, hard-enforced value is a hazard for anyone (human or agent) reading the launcher to understand the actual allowed range.
corrections.fix: Both comments corrected: the preflight description now says 35 items (5 per size, all 7 easy sizes, pointing at get_answer_zebralogic.py's PREFLIGHT_INDICES), and the token-budget comment now says {1024,2048,3072} with a pointer to this amendment file. The top-of-file usage summary's PREFLIGHT line ('5-item format/plumbing check') was also corrected to '35-item (5 per size, all 7 easy sizes)'.
